name: adv_moco_bad
title: MoCo v2 momentum contrast - nine planted defects
note: Momentum contrast is the self-supervised shape with a second, never-trained network - the same structure as a target network in RL, and none of the four defects that decide whether it works at all is modelled by a rule. The MLV301 row is recorded under `unsupported` rather than as a miss because MLView DOES fire - at medium / 0.595, naming `classifier` (a bare nn.Linear, for which eval() changes nothing) instead of `model.query_encoder`, which is the module with the BatchNorm and the dropout. 0.595 is below `mlview.minConfidence` 0.6, so the finding never reaches the VS Code Problems panel. See finding DGRG-22.

expected.defect: nothing seeds torch, numpy or random
expected.why: the RandomResizedCrop and RandomHorizontalFlip that define the two views, the parameter initialisation and the queue order all move between runs

expected.defect: the device names cuda outright with no availability check
expected.why: the script cannot start on a CPU-only machine

expected.defect: the pre-training loader does not shuffle
expected.why: CIFAR-10's file is class-ordered, so every in-batch negative comes from the same few classes and the contrastive task becomes trivial

expected.defect: num_workers=8 with no `if __name__ == "__main__"` guard anywhere in the module - main() is called at module scope on the last line
expected.why: LABEL CORRECTED in hardening round 2 (finding DGRG-20, re-reported as the MLV112 half of the round-2 sweep): `r_data._import_time_chain` now follows the module-scope call chain transitively instead of one hop, so `print(main())` -> `fit()` -> `build_loaders()` is seen for what it is. Original note: MLV112's `_runs_at_import` follows exactly one hop; `build_loader()` is called by `main()`, which is called at module scope. See finding DGRG-20.

expected.defect: the InfoNCE logits are softmaxed before nn.CrossEntropyLoss, which log-softmaxes them again
expected.why: the double softmax flattens the similarity distribution, so the temperature has almost no effect and the representation collapses

expected.defect: the pre-training loop never calls optimizer.zero_grad()
expected.why: every step applies the sum of every batch's gradients since the run started

expected.defect: running_loss is created at line 96, outside the batch loop, and accumulates the live loss tensor
expected.why: the autograd graph of every batch of a 256-wide contrastive pass is retained until the epoch ends, on top of a queue that already holds live tensors

expected.defect: linear_probe() runs both forwards without model.eval()
expected.why: the region is right and the observation is legitimate, so this is not a false positive - but MLView names `classifier` (a bare nn.Linear, for which eval() is a no-op) rather than `model.query_encoder`, which is the module carrying the BatchNorm2d and the Dropout, and the resulting 0.595 is below the Problems-panel floor. Scored neither as a hit nor as a miss; finding DGRG-22 records the defect.

expected.defect: linear_probe() is not wrapped in torch.no_grad()
expected.why: the probe builds a full autograd graph through the frozen encoder for a measurement it never differentiates

expected.defect: the whole MoCo module is pickled instead of its state_dict
expected.why: the checkpoint carries the class path, so it stops loading as soon as the module moves

forbidden.why: optimizer.step() is called at line 107, inside the batch loop
the order in the batch loop is backward (106) then step (107)
there is no torch.no_grad() anywhere in this file - that absence is two of the planted defects
there is no binary cross-entropy in this project
Encoder.__init__ and MoCo.__init__ both call super().__init__() on their first line
there is no train/test split call in this project; self-supervised pre-training has no labelled split
there is no sklearn transformer in this project
the RandomResizedCrop / RandomHorizontalFlip Compose at line 79 is the contrastive augmentation itself, fed to the TRAINING dataset; there is no evaluation transform for it to leak into

unsupported.defect: linear_probe() never calls model.eval(), so the encoder's nn.Dropout(0.1) is active and its BatchNorm2d running statistics keep moving while the probe is measured
unsupported.why: MLView fires MLV301 here at medium / 0.595 naming `classifier` - the bare nn.Linear, for which eval() is a no-op - because `model.query_encoder` is an attribute of a workspace nn.Module and its architecture does not resolve, while `classifier` does. The severity refinement then reads Linear, finds no Dropout or BatchNorm, and de-rates ×0.7 to 0.595, one thousandth below `mlview.minConfidence`. Right region, wrong receiver, wrong severity, invisible in the Problems panel. See finding DGRG-22.

unsupported.defect: the optimizer is built over model.parameters(), which includes the key encoder; the key encoder must only ever be an exponential moving average of the query encoder
unsupported.why: MLV211 (optimizer built over parameters of a model later wrapped or replaced) is the nearest code and is a later-tier rule that is not built; nothing models `an optimizer that owns parameters it must not update`.

unsupported.defect: the key forward is not wrapped in torch.no_grad(), so the key encoder accumulates gradients it must never receive
unsupported.why: no rule models `a frozen branch forwarded with autograd on`; MLV302 only ever looks at an evaluation region, never at a branch inside a training step.

unsupported.defect: the EMA update runs with autograd on and without .data, so the key encoder's parameters become non-leaf tensors and the update is recorded in the graph
unsupported.why: no rule models an in-place parameter update outside no_grad.

unsupported.defect: the negative queue is a plain Python list of live tensors, so every key ever enqueued keeps its autograd graph alive
unsupported.why: MLV205 models an accumulator inside a loop; a queue held on `self` and appended from a method is the same defect in a shape the rule does not reach - `_accumulations` requires the container's binding literal to be `[]` in the accumulating scope.
